title: Marriage Allowance Is Just for Low Earners? Myth… You Could Be Owed £1,260 💍😱 #shorts
description:
Marriage Allowance isn't just for low earners: as a couple you could be owed up to £1,260, and part of it goes next April.

The rule (gov.uk): if you earn less than your Personal Allowance (£12,570), you can transfer £1,260 of it to your husband, wife or civil partner. That cuts their tax by up to £252 a year. Your partner must be a basic-rate taxpayer: income usually up to £50,270 (about £50,000) in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, or up to £43,662 in Scotland (starter, basic or intermediate rate).

The part couples miss: you can backdate a claim to 6 April 2022 (the 2022 to 2023 tax year). HMRC lets you go back up to four years, so with this year that's five tax years at up to £252 each: up to £1,260 in total. Under the four-year limit, 2022 to 2023 can't be claimed after 5 April 2027.

When the myth is true: it's only for married couples and civil partners (living together doesn't count), and not if your partner pays higher or additional rate tax.

Sources: https://www.gov.uk/marriage-allowance · https://taxconfident.campaign.gov.uk/working-life/life-changes/marriage-allowance/ · https://www.gov.uk/income-tax-rates · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/income-tax-personal-allowance-and-the-basic-rate-limit-from-6-april-2022-to-5-april-2026/income-tax-personal-allowance-and-the-basic-rate-limit-from-6-april-2022-to-5-april-2026
